newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-REITER FULFILLS DREAM WITH KITZBUEHEL WIN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-REITER FULFILLS DREAM WITH KITZBUEHEL WIN.

text.p: Austria's Mario Reiter fulfilled one of his biggest ski racing dreams on Sunday by winning the Kitzbuehel men's slalom ahead of Italian superstar Alberto Tomba to the delight of a 40,000 home crowd.
"To win ahead of Tomba is an enormous achievement," said a delighted Reiter.
"Winning Kitzbuehel has always been my dream. I won't be skiing for much longer so it's good I've fulfilled one of my goals aleady. I worked all year for this win, " he added.
Reiter, the 1996 world championship slalom silver medallist, clocked a winning aggregate time of one minute 36.09 seconds on the Ganslern piste, for his third career World Cup win.
He was 0.19 seconds ahead of Tomba, who produced a wild but fast second run to improve on a first-leg fifth place for overall second.
"I am accustomed to winning, it's difficult for me to be second. But today I'm pleased with second place because the conditions in the second run were so bad," said Tomba.
The Italian world and Olympic champion had completed only two of the season's slaloms before Sunday because of wrist and knee injuries which were followed by a bout of flu.
He was second in his first appearance on the circuit in December in Madonna di Campiglio.
On Sunday, Tomba demonstrated he is in good form for his home world championships starting next Sunday in Sestriere.

"Everyone in Italy expects me to do well in Sestriere just because I'm in the race. It's an important event for me," said Tomba, who took slalom and giant slalom gold at last year's world championships in Sierra Nevada.
Reiter's victory came as a surprise as the 26-year-old Austrian had a weak start to the season following health problems he did not want to discuss.
"I am still not 100 percent yet. I was only 80 percent today. The audience gave me the missing 20 percent which I needed for this win," said Reiter.
The 26-year-old Austrian is now anxiously awaiting Sestriere, where he won his only other slalom in a night race last winter.
"I still have two weeks to prepare for world championships. Until today, I was still not qualified. I was the fifth Austrian and only four can participate.

"I am a silver medallist, but now I would like gold medals at world championships and Olympics. But I still think (Austrians Thomas) Sykora and (Thomas) Stangassinger are the favorites for Sestriere."

The in-form Sykora, who was suffering from hip pains after a fall in Sunday morning's free practice, disappointed in the second run and fell back from first place in the opening run to overall seventh.

Last year's winner here, Sykora has won five of the seven slaloms he has stated so far this season and finished second once. It was the first time in a year he had failed to finish on the slalom World Cup rostrum.
"I didn't ski well today. I was too direct going into the gates," said Sykora.
Stangassinger, who finished second three times this season and third twice, fell back a position from a first-run third to fourth.
Norway's Finn Christian Jagge, the 1992 Olympic slalom champion, made his first appearance on a World Cup podium since 1994, with third place on Sunday in 1:36.54.
His compatriot and defending overall World Cup champion Lasse Kjus won the combined event which twinned Sunday's slalom with Saturday's downhill..
Another Norwegian, Kjetil Andre Aamodt was second in the combined to take the lead in the overall standings on 701 points, while Austrian Werner Franz was third.
